specification.problem: Given adjacency-matrix oracle access to an unweighted n-vertex graph G, find a triangle (u,v,w) with all three edges present. The abstract claims query complexity O~(n^{5/4}). The scoped reconstruction is only a small-n (4 to 6) Grover/amplitude-amplification skeleton over vertex triples. It uses the opaque edge oracle, with compute-AND-uncompute of three edge-query bits and a phase-kickback ancilla.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the scaled-down outer Grover search over candidate triples (u,v,w) with an oracle that marks triples whose three edges are present, plus classical verification and repetition. Outside scope: the combinatorial n^{5/4} algorithm itself (random subset sampling, edge-triangle classification, neighborhood search, balancing), the learning-graph comparison, and the lower bounds. Their details are not given in the abstract and are not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: qubits per vertex index, ceil(log2 n)
adjacency bit of the hidden graph
opaque adjacency oracle, one query per placement
triangle indicator A[u][v] AND A[v][w] AND A[u][w], with u,v,w distinct and in [0,n)
size of the search space, 2^{3m} basis states
number of marked basis triples (ordered), unknown

equations.label: Edge oracle
equations.description: Opaque adjacency query, one query per placement.
equations.justification: The sketch gives this adjacency-matrix oracle model; the abstract only implies unweighted edge queries.

equations.label: Triangle predicate
equations.description: Marks the triples that the checker accepts.
equations.abstract_quote: triangle finding problem in unweighted graphs
equations.justification: A triangle in an unweighted graph is three mutually adjacent vertices. The distinctness and range checks are assumed, so the invalid index values (>=n) must be handled.
assumptions: Distinctness and range check done by ordinary gates, with no queries

equations.label: Phase oracle via compute-AND-uncompute
equations.description: Query three edge bits into ancillas, compute AND into a phase-kickback ancilla in |->, then uncompute the edge bits so the ancillas return to |0>. This costs 6 queries per use, 3 to compute and 3 to uncompute.
equations.justification: A standard Grover oracle construction from the sketch, not from the abstract.
assumptions: The ancillas are 3 edge-bit qubits and 1 kickback qubit
The range and distinctness check may need an extra flag ancilla

equations.label: Grover iteration
equations.description: Diffusion about the uniform superposition over triples, applied after the phase oracle.
equations.justification: Standard Grover search, used as the scaled-down skeleton of amplitude amplification.
assumptions: Uniform superposition over all 2^{3m} index strings, including invalid ones, which U_f leaves unmarked

equations.label: Success probability and iteration count
equations.description: Success probability after k iterations. If M is unknown, try k=1,2,4,... with verification after each try.
equations.justification: Standard amplitude amplification, matching the sketch's 1/sqrt(p) iteration count and the exponential guessing of iteration counts.
assumptions: M>=1 for a graph that contains a triangle

registers.name: e
registers.role: edge-bit ancillas for A[u][v], A[v][w], A[u][w], returned to 0

registers.name: flag
registers.role: optional validity (distinct, <n) flag ancilla, returned to 0

specification.initial_state: All qubits in |0>. Hadamard on u,v,w to give the uniform superposition. The kick ancilla is set to |->.

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition on the three vertex registers and put the kickback ancilla in |->.
Apply the phase oracle. Compute the 3 edge bits with O_G placeholders, check validity, and compute the AND into kick. Then uncompute everything so the ancillas return to 0.
Apply the diffusion on the u,v,w registers. Repeat for k iterations, with k chosen via the exponential guessing schedule.
Measure the u,v,w registers, taking care over little-endian bit order, and verify the result classically.

specification.measurement: Measure only the u,v,w registers (3m bits). In Qiskit counts keys the last character is classical bit 0. Map each register to its own classical bits and decode carefully.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Decode (u,v,w), check distinctness and that each index is <n, and verify with three direct edge queries. If verification fails, repeat with another k from the guessing schedule, O(log n) repetitions in total.
assumptions: Scaled-down instance: n in 4..6, so 3m=6 or 9 index qubits plus 5 ancillas, within the cap only if the cap allows it
Ordered triples are searched, so M=6 times the number of triangles
This is not the paper's n^{5/4} algorithm and has about n^{3/2} query cost, only a skeleton
missing_information: The abstract gives no details of the combinatorial algorithm: subset size, sampling, classification of edges by triangle count, or the neighborhood search
The exact outer amplitude-amplification structure and parameter balancing for n^{5/4} are not given
The qubit cap and the query budget are unknown
